# Release Notes v0.7.0

**Released:** 2026-10-13

This release puts the daemon in charge of telling you why your lights are not behaving. It detects competing RGB software and names the fix, admits when a config write did not reach disk, and reports whether the Windows SMBus broker is actually running. Alongside that, the network trust model is rebuilt around credentials rather than locality, the web UI moves wholesale to pointer events so drag surfaces work under touch and pen, and LightScript effects can now read device touches and buttons.

## 🌟 Highlights

### ✨ The daemon finds the RGB software fighting it for your hardware
A new catalog (`crates/hypercolor-core/src/device/conflicts/catalog.toml`) matches running processes and services against known RGB tools, and the daemon rescans every 30 seconds plus on device errors and discovery completion. `GET /api/v1/system/conflicts` reads the latest scan and `POST /api/v1/system/conflicts/scan` forces a fresh one; both return `SoftwareConflictsStatus`. The Devices page shows a `SoftwareConflictBanner` naming each program, the scope it competes over, the exact remedy ("Quit iCUE from its tray icon, then stop the Corsair Service in services.msc"), and the process names that matched. Device cards carry a one-line hint, and the Windows SMBus support card warns separately for any program with `smbus: true`. Process enumeration reads `/proc/<pid>/comm` and `/cmdline` on Linux and queries `Win32_Process` plus running `Win32_Service` on Windows; interpreter launches (`python`, `node`, `java`, and friends) are matched by script name. The desktop app's old Tauri-side detector is retired, so every client sees the same answer.

### 🔒 Network trust is decided by credential, not by where the packet came from
A loopback peer that forwards headers no longer gets ambient control: `request_is_loopback()` now treats any relayed request as remote, so a reverse proxy relaying an internet client cannot inherit keyless trust. Keyless requests must also name the daemon by an admitted name; the new `HostAllowlist` in `crates/hypercolor-daemon/src/api/host_names.rs` admits IP literals, `localhost` and its subdomains, `network.allowed_hosts`, hostnames from `web.cors_origins`, the machine's own names, and the mDNS name, and refuses anything else with 403 and `details.setting = "network.allowed_hosts"`. Public routes now run fully anonymous with no loopback locality, closing an ambient-authority path for local browsers. See Breaking changes.

### 🤖 Downstream builds can supply their own credentials
`CredentialAuthority` in `crates/hypercolor-daemon/src/api/credential_authority.rs` lets a downstream build resolve bearer tokens to a `CredentialGrant` carrying a `CredentialTier` (`Read` or `Control`), a non-secret `credential_id`, and a revocation token. Grants are clamped to the authority's `ceiling()` and never carry protected control, which stays with operator credentials. Revocation reaches live WebSocket sessions: every send races the token, and a revoked session closes with **code 1008 (`close_code::POLICY`)** and reason `credential revoked` on every exit path, with a one second `REVOKED_CLOSE_DEADLINE` so the courtesy frame cannot hold the socket open.

### ✨ Effects can read device touches and buttons
LightScript gains `engine.touch` and `engine.deviceButtons`. `TouchContact` carries `device`, `contact`, `x`, `y`, `pressure`, and a `canvas` point when the device is placed on the render zone's layout; `DeviceButtonHold` carries `device` and `button`. `DeviceSurfaceMap` (`crates/hypercolor-core/src/spatial/device_surface.rs`) places a device on the canvas only when exactly one LED output in the zone routes to it, then maps surface coordinates through the output's placement, mirroring, and edge behavior, so the same finger lands at different canvas points in zones with different layouts. A new **Touch Ripple** effect ships in the SDK for the ROLI Lightpad and other touch surfaces: held contacts glow with pressure, each landing throws a ripple from its canvas point, and device buttons step the palette.

### 📱 Drag surfaces work under touch and pen
`crates/hypercolor-ui/src/pointer_gesture.rs` introduces a single-pointer gesture model (`PointerGesture`, `GestureEnd`, `PointerEnd`, `HeldButtons`, `capture_pointer`, `holds_capture`) and the color wheel, resize handles, Studio editor panels, layout boxes, the viewport picker, and the interactive canvas preview all move onto it. Mouse, pen, and touch follow one code path with pointer capture, so drags keep tracking outside bounds and a lost capture reverts the interaction instead of leaving it stuck. Touch presses keep their browser defaults so double-tap still fires `dblclick`, popovers dismiss on `pointerdown`, and the window listeners these surfaces used to install are removed on cleanup.

## 🔧 Daemon, API, and networking

- **`--port`** moves the listening port for one launch without pinning interfaces. The config's `network.access_mode` still picks interfaces, loopback stays reachable on that port when the config names a specific interface, and an unavailable configured address degrades to loopback rather than aborting. `--port` and `--bind` together are rejected.
- **Keyless listener warning at startup** fires only when there is no API key, no control-granting authority, the API binds off loopback, *and* the policy actually admits a remote client in some address family. A custom scope that lists no clients produces no warning.
- WebSocket upgrades are admitted for credentialed clients from any origin and for pages the daemon serves itself (`is_own_origin`), alongside loopback and trusted Tauri origins. Commands replayed on a session carry the session's grant and keep an anonymous loopback session's standing.
- Extensions can no longer declare public routes inside the MCP mount, and a refused declaration does not receive the docs bearer exemption.
- CORS headers are sent to bracketed IPv6 loopback origins.
- The desktop app's bundled daemon now follows the configured network mode. See Upgrade notes.
- `software_conflicts_changed` is added to `protocol/websocket-v1.json`; the event carries `{ count }`.

## ⚙️ Config persistence honesty

- `ConfigPersistence` (`Durable` or `Lagging { path, error }`) is reported through `ConfigManager::persistence_status()`.
- `ConfigMutationResponse` gains **`persisted`** (defaults to `true` when absent) and **`persistence_error`**. Handlers that saved report their own outcome; paths that did not save report the manager's current status.
- `hypercolor config set` and `config reset` print a warning instead of a success line when a change is live but did not reach disk, and say when a restart is safe. The exit code stays 0 because the change did take effect.
- `hypercolor diagnose` warns while the config file lags the live config, and a lagging file keeps its error until a write lands. A stale retry can no longer overwrite a capture commit.

## 🪟 Windows hardware support

- The SMBus broker logs its full lifecycle to `logs\smbus-broker.log` beside its executable: version, pid, module resolution, status transitions, control codes, and the first failure of each kind.
- `broker_service_status()` returns a `BrokerServiceStatus` with `state`, `win32_exit_code`, `service_specific_exit_code` (1 = request loop failed, 2 = runtime teardown failed), `starts_at_boot`, `log_path`, `answering`, and `version`.
- `hardware_broker_check()` fails diagnose when the broker is installed but stopped, warns when it is missing, transitioning, or not answering, and passes when it answers or is not needed.
- Installer fixes: hardware setup runs in 64-bit PowerShell, the broker is registered even when PawnIO setup fails, the user is told when the broker does not start, and the setup log is kept when it cannot be rotated.
- Broker robustness: the image path is unquoted, a pipeless broker fails fast, a pipe flood no longer stops the service, and a squatted pipe is waited out instead of treated as fatal.
- The Windows diagnostics probe reports conflicts, USB bindings, and scan state.

## 🐛 Devices and drivers

- **USB HID**: top-level collections are enumerated, USB functions with no lighting-capable interface are dropped, and HID functions carrying only consumer controls are hidden, so the unclaimed-device list stops advertising things Hypercolor cannot light.
- Hotplug arrivals no longer join partial HID data.
- **Lian Li wireless**: the watchdog probes returning receivers and waits out the full probe response interval before resetting TX; wireless TX stays on the discovered fan channel instead of falling back to channel 1; fans discovered after an empty reconnect are recovered via `request_reconnection()`; receiver absence is judged from the last sighting rather than the current clock, and probe budget renewal is bounded across brief table omissions.

## ⚡️ Effect runtime

- **servo-script 0.6.0 is vendored** under `vendor/servo-script/` and patched for two memory problems that no Servo release carries yet. `set_script_source_private()` reclaims the caller's reference after the engine takes its own, fixing a leak of one `ModuleScript` per compiled script; and the script thread now runs a full `JS_GC` once evaluation traffic lasts 60 seconds or compiles 16 MiB of source without a major GC in between, since Servo has no idle or periodic collection and a page evaluating once per frame could run for hours while garbage accumulated.
- `scripts/check-vendored-patches.sh` runs in CI and fails when a `[patch.crates-io]` entry stops resolving to its `vendor/` copy, so a dependency bump cannot silently ship the unpatched crate.
- LightScript re-sends the interaction batch after an edge frame.
- `servo-allocator` is pinned back to Servo's version so jemalloc links.

## 🔔 Release notifications

The OSS daemon binary installs `OssUpdateInstaller`, which registers a release-notification service as extension state, an API extension, and a lifecycle hook. Downstream distributors omit it and the feature does not exist in their builds. Endpoints are `GET` and `PATCH /api/v1/release-notifications` and `POST /api/v1/release-notifications/check`. Automatic checks run every **24 hours** (`CHECK_INTERVAL`) and retry after **15 minutes** (`FAILURE_RETRY_INTERVAL`) on failure, with state in `ConfigManager::state_dir().join("release-notifications.json")`. Drafts, prereleases, and releases not newer than the running version are skipped outright. A release with no matching download asset for the current platform is still reported, just without a download link. If the state file is unreadable, settings stay available with automatic checks disabled so recovery cannot override a previous opt-out.

## 📝 Documentation

- New and corrected pages on competing-software detection, Export Diagnostics, the `scan_failed` state and the container blind spot, credential authorities and public routes, the WebSocket origin change, LAN and bind behavior, MCP and CORS statements, and the persisted-config contract with its capture exception.
- Bug report templates accept attachments and list the new diagnose check.
- `ROADMAP.md` points near-term work at the 0.7.0 milestone with corrected hardware research counts and headset status; `CHANGELOG.md` drops `cargo install` advice for the unpublished CLI and folds a stale Unreleased section into 0.4.0.
- Specs 75, 80, and 82 record the pointer migration waves, probe-gated pacing rules, and phase 2 of device input.

## 💥 Breaking changes

- **Relayed loopback requests lose ambient trust.** A reverse proxy on loopback that forwards a remote client no longer receives keyless control. Give the proxy a credential, or set `allow_unauthenticated_remote_access` deliberately.
- **Keyless requests must name an admitted host.** If you reach the daemon through a DNS name that is not an IP literal, a `localhost` form, a configured CORS origin host, the machine's own name, or the mDNS name, add it to `network.allowed_hosts` or the request is refused with 403.
- **Public routes no longer report loopback locality.** `context.is_loopback()` is false on public routes; handlers that branched on it must use credentials instead.
- **Extensions cannot declare public routes under the MCP mount.** Such declarations are refused, and a refused declaration also loses the docs bearer exemption.
- **The desktop app's bundled daemon now follows the configured network mode.** An existing LAN setting opens that daemon on upgrade where it previously stayed local.
- **`ConfigMutationResponse` gained fields.** Clients deserializing it strictly need to accept `persisted` and `persistence_error`; `persisted` defaults to `true` when absent.

## 🔼 Upgrade notes

- Review `network.access_mode` before launching the desktop app after upgrading. If a LAN mode is set, the app's daemon will now listen on the network; set `HYPERCOLOR_API_KEY` or switch to `lan_protected` if that is not what you want. The daemon logs a startup warning naming each keyless network listener.
- If you front the daemon with a reverse proxy, issue it a credential. Relayed requests no longer inherit loopback trust.
- Add any custom DNS names you use to reach the daemon to `network.allowed_hosts`.
- On Windows, run `hypercolor diagnose` after upgrading. The new hardware broker check will tell you if the SMBus broker is installed but not running, and points at `logs\smbus-broker.log` beside the broker executable.
- Scripted `hypercolor config set` callers should check the new `persisted` field (or the warning line) rather than assuming a zero exit code means the change hit disk.
- If competing RGB software warnings appear on the Devices page, follow the per-program remedy; dismissals persist until that program stops and starts again.
- Building from source: `vendor/servo-script/` is now part of the tree and patched. Do not bump `servo` or `servo-script` without re-vendoring; `scripts/check-vendored-patches.sh` will fail the build if the patch stops applying.
